newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman unworried about Tenn. Karnal bunt.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman unworried about Tenn. Karnal bunt.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman Thursday said he was not concerned about the recent discovery of the fungus Karnal bunt in wheat in Tennessee.

"This does not concern me. It's very contained, it's location is contained and it does not appear to be in any danger of spread whatsoever," Glickman told reporters after addressing the Washington Research Group.
The secretary said he was not surprised USDA's nationwide survey had turned up the fungus.
"I'm not surpised we're finding it in a few areas," Glickman said. "Where we're finding it indicates to me that it's not a widespread phenomenon."
Last week Tennessee agriculture officials said a grain sample taken from a farm bin in Giles county tested positive for the fungus and samples from seven other counties were believed to be positive.
The news triggered fears karnal bunt might surface in other growing areas and pushed wheat futures prices down.
